sn35.129:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park.
sn35.129:1.2: Then the householder Ghosita approached the Venerable Ānanda … and said to him:
sn35.129:1.3: “Venerable Ānanda, it is said, ‘diversity of elements, diversity of elements.’
sn35.129:1.4: In what way, venerable sir, has the diversity of elements been spoken of by the Blessed One?”
sn35.129:1.5: “Householder, there exists the eye element, and forms that are agreeable, and eye-consciousness:
sn35.129:1.6: in dependence on a contact to be experienced as pleasant, a pleasant feeling arises.
sn35.129:1.7: There exists the eye element, and forms that are disagreeable, and eye-consciousness:
sn35.129:1.8: in dependence on a contact to be experienced as painful, a painful feeling arises.
sn35.129:1.9: There exists the eye element, and forms that are a basis for equanimity, and eye-consciousness:
sn35.129:1.10: in dependence on a contact to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant, a neither- painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises.
sn35.129:1.11: “Householder, there exists the ear element … the nose element … the tongue element … the body element …
sn35.129:1.17: the mind element, and mental phenomena that are agreeable, and mind-consciousness:
sn35.129:1.18: in dependence on a contact to be experienced as pleasant, a pleasant feeling arises.
sn35.129:1.19: There exists the mind element, and mental phenomena that are disagreeable, and mind-consciousness:
sn35.129:1.20: in dependence on a contact to be experienced as painful, a painful feeling arises.
sn35.129:1.21: There exists the mind element, and mental phenomena that are a basis for equanimity, and mind-consciousness:
sn35.129:1.22: in dependence on a contact to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant, a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises.
sn35.129:1.23: “It is in this way, householder, that the diversity of elements has been spoken of by the Blessed One.”
